text:
Maya: Heads-up — onboarding atlas-30b-int4 for long-context (target 64k+). Quick smoke shows tokens drifting after ~48k and occasional token duplication when we stream kvs across shard boundary.

Jon: Duplication as in repeated tokens in output or in kv-index histogram?

Maya: Repeated tokens in output. Small example attached: prompt seeds -> at 48,128 tokens the model emits a short repeated phrase then continues. Not catastrophic but reproducible across seeds.

Linh: Which kv mode? interleaved or contiguous? Any sharding enabled?

Maya: Default: kv_shard=round_robin, kv_pack=int4, rope_mode=scale_adapt, max_ctx=65536. Run on dedicated c6g-gpu pool, batch=1, streaming=false.

robo-ci: test/5187659998: atlas-30b-int4-longctx-smoke queued. 5/9 seeds completed so far. Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/onboard/5187659998/

Jon: Can you paste a minimal repro prompt? Also include a binary checksum of the kv entries around the boundary (like md5 of kv-pages 0..10).

Maya: Minimal: "[A]_repeat_10000 + instruction: continue story". I added a small checker that dumps md5 per kv-page every 4k tokens. Logs show two consecutive pages with identical md5 at the 48k mark.

Linh: Identical md5 implies a stale write or memcpy copy bug. Two ideas: allocator page reuse without invalidate, or a race in kv-eviction that writes zeroes then rewrites old data. Any allocator churn metrics?

Maya: Allocator shows frequent free/alloc cycles around token 46k-49k, and pageflip count spikes. Also observed memcpy spikes and an unexpected barrier in the code path: `compact_and_rotate_pages()` called when active_pages > threshold.

Jon: Can you try forcing `kv_shard=contiguous` + `no_compact=true` and re-run single seed to see if duplication disappears? If so, compaction path is suspect.

Maya: Will run that. Also toggled rope_mode to `clip_scale=0.995` in a separate run to check if RoPE drift contributes to token repeat.

robo-ci: run started: 5187659998-A (contiguous,no_compact), ETA 8m

Linh: If it's allocator reuse, we should see identical pointer addresses in the kv dumps. Can you add a pointer+md5 dump (address, md5) for pages N-2..N+2 at the boundary?

Maya: Added pointer dump. Early read shows same pointer reused at N and N+1 with same md5 — suspicious. Will share artifacts.

Jon: Also compare fp16 baseline on same prompt to ensure duplication isn't a model-level behavior. If fp16 doesn't duplicate, it's runtime/kv related.

Maya: FP16 baseline (same infra) completed 3/3 seeds: no duplication at 48k. So likely runtime.

robo-ci: artifact: s3://redwood-artifacts/onboard/5187659998/ (kv_page_md5.csv, pointer_dump.log, perf.json, outputs.tgz)

Linh: Nice. Next hypothesis: compact path does an in-place memcpy with overlapping src/dst, but uses memcpy (not memmove) causing corruption when overlap occurs. Search code for memcpy in compaction.

Jon: I'll open a quick PR that replaces memcpy->memmove in compaction and add a unit test for overlapping pages. If that fixes it, we'll schedule a runtime patch.

Maya: Patch test queued locally. Also tried contiguous+no_compact run — so far no repeats in first 60k tokens.

robo-ci: 5187659998-A: success (1/1 seed), latency ~210ms/token at 60k, no duplication observed.

Linh: Great. Can you also collect quality diffs at 60k (logprob mean, top1 changes) between int4-no_compact and fp16? We need to ensure quantization itself isn't creating subtle drift.

Maya: Will run goldset at 60k checkpoint. Quick numbers earlier: int4 baseline perplexity +3.2% vs fp16 at 5k, but at 60k with no_compact it's +4.1% (still within threshold but worth tracking).

Jon: OK. Action items: (1) Jon to PR memcpy->memmove + unit test, (2) Maya to run matrix: {kv_shard: [round_robin, contiguous], compaction: [on,off], rope_mode: [scale_adapt,clip_scale=0.995]} x 2 seeds, collect pointer/md5 + goldset diffs, (3) Linh to draft runtime bug if memcpy overlap confirmed.

Maya: Adding OpsBot note to schedule canary on dedicated pool if PR passes tests.

OpsBot: Canary scheduled: runtime-compaction-memmove on pool "dedicated-c6g" after CI merge.

Maya: Thanks team. Will post full artifact links and summary when matrix finishes. :mag_right:
